conventions.convention: Quaternions use Hamilton multiplication, ij=k, jk=i, ki=j. N(q) is the squared Euclidean norm, a real number; real scalars are embedded as (r,0,0,0).
φ identifies the ordered spatial coordinates with (i,j,k); ρ(q) acts by x↦qxq⁻¹. Its matrix is taken in the ordered imaginary basis (i,j,k).
Body angular velocity satisfies RᵀR′z=ω×z and R′=RΩω. Thus the quaternion equation multiplies the imaginary rate on the right: q′=(1/2)qφ(ω).
The differential results use nondegenerate open real intervals; rotation paths are entrywise C¹ and prescribed angular velocities need only be continuous.
The imported covering conclusion is used under ACω, including its surjectivity, kernel {1,−1}, and two-preimage assertion.
For the closed-loop counterexample, C¹ on [0,1] means continuous on [0,1] and C¹ on (0,1), without endpoint derivatives.
For the constant-rate closed loop, C¹ on [0,T] means continuity on the closed interval and C¹ regularity on its interior; T=2π/|ω₀| is used only when ω₀≠0.

load_bearing.statement: S³={q∈H:N(q)=1}; φ:R³→Im H identifies the ordered vector coordinates with (i,j,k); ρ(q)=c_q|Im H with c_q(x)=qxq⁻¹. A quaternion lift of R:I→SO(3) is q:I→S³ with ρ(q(t))=R(t). Under the cited ACω hypothesis, ρ:S³→SO(3) is a surjective two-sheeted covering homomorphism with kernel {1,−1}.

For C¹ quaternion and 3×3 matrix curves on a nondegenerate open interval, (pq)′=p′q+pq′ and (AB)′=A′B+AB′. For all p,q∈H, conjugation reverses products, N(pq)=N(p)N(q), and Re(p q̄)=⟨p,q⟩₂. For q=a+φ(u), qφ(v)q̄=φ((a²−‖u‖₂²)v+2⟨u,v⟩₂u+2a(u×v)); the unit half-angle specialization gives the stated Rodrigues formula.

Let I be a nondegenerate open interval and ω:I→R³ continuous. Every C¹ solution of q′=(1/2)qφ(ω) has constant N(q); a solution with one unit value stays in S³ and gives a C¹ rotation path R=ρ∘q with R′=RΩω. For every t₀∈I and q₀∈S³, the IVP has exactly one maximal solution and its domain is all of I.

For a C¹ path R:I→SO(3) on a nondegenerate open interval, Ω=RᵀR′ is skew-symmetric, there is exactly one continuous ω with Ωz=ω×z for all z∈R³, and R′=RΩω. The displayed coordinate formula is ω=(−Ω₂₃,Ω₁₃,−Ω₁₂).

Let I be a nondegenerate open interval, R:I→SO(3) C¹, t₀∈I, and q₀∈S³ with ρ(q₀)=R(t₀). There is exactly one C¹ lift q with q(t₀)=q₀, namely the solution q′=(1/2)qφ(ω_R). Every C¹ lift equals q or −q. The Remarks retain the imported ACω hypothesis.
For C¹ q:I→S³ on a nondegenerate open interval, q⁻¹q′ is imaginary and ω=2φ⁻¹(q⁻¹q′) is continuous. The path q satisfies q′=(1/2)qφ(ω), and R=ρ∘q is C¹ with R′=RΩω, so ω is its body angular velocity.

concerns.concern: Statement clause 2 gives ω=(−Ω₂₃,Ω₁₃,−Ω₁₂), and proof 1.2 uses Ω₁₁ and vector coordinates z₁,z₂,z₃. The cited def-matrix-space explicitly defines 3×3 matrices on {0,1,2}×{0,1,2} and says both indices start at 0. Thus Ω₂₃ and Ω₁₃ are undefined under the supplied definition. No one-based entry relabeling is stated. The intended cross-product formula is correct after an explicit relabeling, but the displayed statement is ill-typed as written.

The Definition writes φ(v₁,v₂,v₃)=v₁i+v₂j+v₃k while identifying its domain with R³ of def-euclidean-inner-product, whose function coordinates are indexed 0,1,2. A local convention identifying the three displayed tuple positions with those function coordinates is missing. This convention also matters for the product lemma's sums from 1 to 3 and the examples' basis names e₁,e₂,e₃.

Proof 1.2 concludes that N∘q is constant from its zero derivative without citing the zero-derivative theorem, which is absent from deps. This is an immediate mean-value-theorem consequence on the stated open interval, but the exact logical supplier is omitted.

The second Remark introduces the homomorphism, two-preimage, and antipodal assertions with 'Equivalently' after the smooth two-sheeted covering conclusion. Those assertions alone do not express the local covering-sheet property. They are consequences of the imported conclusion; the word 'Equivalently' overstates what the abbreviated list records.

alerts.finding: The Definition quantifies over 'every compact time-state cylinder C⊆D' and 'every compact time-state-parameter cylinder C⊆D_Λ' without defining either cylinder class or citing its definition. This matters because the local continuation supplier uses closed-ball state cylinders, whereas the assigned quaternion lemma explicitly supplies its own compact-product convention in F7. The published definition itself leaves the quantified class unspecified.

The Statement says ACω is 'used only to select the initial unit quaternion ... through the surjectivity of the double cover'. The opened covering supplier ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism instead states in A1 and Verification 1.2 that ACω is used through the closed-subgroup construction of SO(3); Verification 3.1 and 4.1 distinguish the finite choices from that hypothesis. Choosing one preimage of one given rotation is not itself a countable-choice use. The hypothesis is retained, but its stated use is inaccurate.

The Statement says ACω is 'used only to select initial unit quaternions through the double cover'. The opened covering supplier locates its ACω use in the closed-subgroup construction of SO(3), not the finite selection of an initial preimage. The consuming construction is otherwise faithful, but this description of the inherited choice cost is inaccurate.
